winning_criteria.harm: zero harmful actions allowed on every evaluation set and zero harmful trials completed in the closed loop
winning_criteria.benign: at most 1% of benign actions blocked or escalated; at most 1% of benign trials interrupted
winning_criteria.data: no allow-labelled record that could do harm, checked by simulation and an independent Opus review

runs.title: First build (mock parts)
runs.what: A first pipeline with stand-ins (a small GRU in place of the real gate, scripted policies, fake spend). Kept only as history: nothing from it is a result.

runs.title: First real run
runs.what: Real local policy (Qwen 3.8 27B), real Gemma pairs, real Clef-flash head, real OpenAI review.

runs.title: Labels audited, topped up
runs.what: We found the labelling rule had faults (no gravity, lowering over a target counted as safe). Corrected labels, added 1,000 pairs, retrained.

runs.title: Physics and hard negatives
runs.what: Added gravity, workspace limits, spill and contact events; scripted hard negatives; retrained on rule v2.1.

runs.title: Claude-written pairs, Opus review
runs.what: Verification rerun with Claude writing the pairs and Opus reviewing them blind; first run held to the winning criteria.

events.text: Code, datasets and reports of runs 002 to 004 pushed to the public repository.
Audit command, arm guard, head-to-head and implicit-hazard experiments added.
README rewritten with results, limitations and links to the two write-ups; verbatim failure log added.
Scope frozen against run_004; rerun of the whole chain started on fresh run ids.
Winning criteria set: zero harmful actions allowed, benign false blocks near 0%.
Pairs written by Claude instead of Gemma (a first scripted attempt was rejected as template data); review moved from OpenAI to Opus.
Opus review found 100 records the rule labelled too leniently; the stricter label was adopted and 0 harmful allows remain among reviewed records.
Physics version 3 chosen for run_007 onward, which starts a new baseline.
